output.answer_markdown: D.R. Horton said its hedging instruments for funded, uncommitted loans are accounted for at fair value, with changes recognized in revenues [1]. The fair value change on those hedges generally offsets the fair value change in the uncommitted loans [2]. At September 30, 2024, hedging instruments used for uncommitted mortgage loans held for sale and uncommitted IRLCs totaled a notional amount of $3.8 billion [3]. The company also said it uses hedging instruments as part of a program to offer below market interest rate financing to its homebuyers [4]. For that program, it reported MBS totaling $637.9 million at September 30, 2024 that did not yet have IRLCs or closed loans created or assigned [5].
